questions.knowledge_point: Solving for One Coefficient in a Linear Combination
questions.problem:
Find $k$, if $3{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2}=0$ and 

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $k$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2} & =0 \\ 3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+k[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ k[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ k[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the first components, we get 

$$
3k=-6\,⟹\,k=-2.
$$

But then

$$
\begin{aligned}-2[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\ne [\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there is no $k$ such that $3{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2}=0.$

questions.problem:
Find $k$, if $8{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2}=0$ and

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 6 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $k$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2} & =0 \\ 8[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 6 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+k[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ k[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 6 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ k[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}24 \\ -48 \\ 32\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the first components, we get 

$$
-2k=24\,⟹\,k=-12.
$$

But then 

$$
\begin{aligned}-12[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}24 \\ -36 \\ 48\end{aligned}]\ne [\begin{aligned}24 \\ -48 \\ 32\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there is no $k$ such that 
 $8{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2}=0.$

$$

Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $h$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}+h{a}_{2} & =b \\ 3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+h[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ h[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ h[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 4 \\ 8 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Find $x$, if $2a+4x=b$ and

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ 6\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}14 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2a+4x & =b \\ 4x & =b-2a \\ x & =\frac{1}{4}(b-2a) \\ x & =\frac{1}{4}([\begin{aligned}14 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]) \\ x & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ -4 \\ -12\end{aligned}] \\ x & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination
questions.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=7 \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=9 \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=4\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the third equation by $-1$ and adding the result to the first equation we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{1} & =7-4 \\ {x}_{1} & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now,  we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ into the third equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} & =4 \\ 3(3)-{x}_{2} & =4 \\ -{x}_{2} & =4-9 \\ {x}_{2} & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=5$ into the second equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & =9 \\ -2(3)+3(5) & =9 \\ -6+15 & =9,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=5,$ which means

$$
3{a}_{1}+5{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3+5=8.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -11 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
.
questions.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -11 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -11 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -11 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=3 \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-11 \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the second and the third  equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8{x}_{1} & =-16\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=-2$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4(-2)+{x}_{2}=-5\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2}=3$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & =3 \\ (-2)+2(3) & =3 \\ 4 & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement. 

So, the system has no solution.

{c}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}].

$$

$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

questions.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-3 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=1 \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the resulting equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =-5,\end{aligned}
$$

which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=1 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3(-5) & =1 \\ -2{x}_{1} & =-14 \\ {x}_{1} & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=7$ and ${x}_{2}=-5$ into the third equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=-4 \\ 3(7)+5(-5) & =-4 \\ -4 & =-4,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=7$ and ${x}_{2}=-5,$ which means

$$
7{a}_{1}-5{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=7+(-5)=2.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-7 \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-1 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=6\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the first and the second equation we get

$$
-2{x}_{2}=-8\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=4.
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=4$ into the first equation yields

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} & =-7 \\ {x}_{1}-(4) & =-7 \\ {x}_{1} & =-7+4 \\ {x}_{1} & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & =6 \\ 2(-3)+3(4) & =6 \\ 6 & =6,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=4,$ which means

$$
-3{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-3+4=1.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination
questions.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -9 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -9 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -9 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -9 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-1 \\ 3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-9 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-1 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-3 \\ {x}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+(-1)=-3\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-2.
$$

Finally, by substituting ${x}_{2}=-2,{x}_{3}=-1$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} & =-1 \\ {x}_{1}+(-2)+3(-1) & =-1 \\ {x}_{1}-5 & =-1 \\ {x}_{1} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=4$, ${x}_{2}=-2$, and ${x}_{3}=-1,$ which means 

$$
4{a}_{1}-2{a}_{2}-{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=4+(-2)-(-1)=3.
$$

Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -21 \\ -12\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 14 \\ 9\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -21 \\ -12\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 14 \\ 9\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ -5{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4{x}_{2} \\ -21{x}_{2} \\ -12{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{3} \\ 14{x}_{3} \\ 9{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} \\ -5{x}_{1}-21{x}_{2}+14{x}_{3} \\ -3{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=2 \\ -5{x}_{1}-21{x}_{2}+14{x}_{3}=8 \\ -3{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3}=-7\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -3 & 2 \\ -5 & -21 & 14 & 8 \\ -3 & -12 & 9 & -7\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -3 & 2 \\ -5 & -21 & 14 & 8 \\ -3 & -12 & 9 & -7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 18 \\ -3 & -12 & 9 & -7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 18 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=2 \\ -{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=18 \\ 0=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0=-1$  gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination
questions.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{3} \\ -11{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ -2{x}_{2}-11{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=5 \\ -2{x}_{2}-11{x}_{3}=-18 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & -15 & -30\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{15}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=5 \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-6 \\ {x}_{3}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting this value into  the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}-2(2)=-6\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-2.
$$

 

Finally, by substituting ${x}_{2}=-2$ and ${x}_{3}=2$ into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} & =5 \\ {x}_{1}+(-2)+3(2) & =5 \\ {x}_{1}+4 & =5 \\ {x}_{1} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=1$, ${x}_{2}=-2$, and ${x}_{3}=2,$ which means 

$$
{a}_{1}-2{a}_{2}+2{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1+(-2)+2=1.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ -2{x}_{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3}=8 \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-6 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=2\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & -20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3}=8 \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-6 \\ {x}_{3}=5.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=5.$ Substituting this value in the second and first equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}_{2}-2(5)=-6\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=4 \\  & {x}_{1}+5=8\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=3$, ${x}_{2}=4$, and ${x}_{3}=5,$ which means 

$$
3{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}+5{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=3+4+5=12.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination
questions.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ 6\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 9\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -6 \\ 7\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ 6\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 9\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -6 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2} \\ 6{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ 9{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -6 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -6 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-2 \\ 2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=-6 \\ 3{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3}=7\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 & -6 \\ 3 & 6 & 9 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 & -6 \\ 3 & 6 & 9 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -2 \\ 3 & 6 & 9 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 13\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-2 \\ {x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=-2 \\ 0=13.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0=13$  gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $s$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}+s{a}_{2} & =b \\ 3[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 6 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ s[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 6 \\ -5\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ s[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}16 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From the final equation above, we can tell that $s=4.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}a+2x & =b \\ 2x & =b-a \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}(b-a) \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}([\begin{aligned}24 \\ -9 \\ 13\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}12 \\ -11 \\ -5\end{aligned}]) \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 2 \\ 18\end{aligned}] \\ x & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 1 \\ 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the vectors

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042052/assets/e9e0ea8fb6e9ba5f4595f15efe4f04e93db373dbc020f5672db34d5a3c12024b.png)

If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2  = \mathbf d,$ then what is $x_1+x_2?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2  = \mathbf d,$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=5 \\ -{x}_{1}=-5 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we obtain $x_1=5,$ which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =5 \\ 4(5)+{x}_{2} & =5 \\ {x}_{2} & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x_1=5$ and $x_2=-15$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =0 \\ 3(5)+(-15) & =0 \\ 0 & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is $x_1=5$ and $x_2=-15,$ which means

$$
5 \mathbf{c_1}-15 \mathbf{c_2} = \mathbf{d}.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_1+x_2=5-15=-10.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the vectors

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042052/assets/4749f1e50cf7768f39d26737bfce4d9e8e85d5b350f4bc9844a358cd4c3c5cc0.png)

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since $\mathbf{b}$ is a linear combination of vectors $\mathbf{a_1}, \,\mathbf{a_2}$ and $\mathbf{a_3}$ with coefficients $x_1,\, x_2$ and $x_3,$ respectively, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 \\ {x}_{1} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ -{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=1 \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=7\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042052/assets/a4e5c5eba6d2d8b30955668d47bb2a131c702cc7ec62ef7dada9ed9ad60d8182.png)

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{3}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3 = 2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
x_2+(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2 = -1,
$$

and substituting $x_3=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x_1+2(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1 = -3.
$$

So the solution of the system is $x_1=-3, x_2=-1, x_3=2,$ which means

$$
-3 \mathbf{a_1}- \mathbf{a_2} +2 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_1+x_2+x_3=-3-1+2=-2.
$$
